page_title: Web-based configuration and installation of ADAS camera
page_content:
[TOC]


### Prerequisites:
- The device and the computer are on the same LAN segment, and the computer can successfully ping the device's local IP address.
- Alternatively, if the device has a WiFi module, switch it to AP mode; the computer connects to the AP hotspot and accesses the address `192.168.42.100`.
- The device is in the factory-ready state (AI is authorized, and algorithms are loaded).

### Flowchart
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=64cc8c8fc05d4db67c73a5ad40c18ce4)

### Physical Image
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=8ca18fa64a80b7409c5a347a47535b7a)

### Operation Steps:
###### 1. Camera Installation
1.1 The optimal installation position is at the intersection of the vehicle's central axis and the horizontal line above the windshield wipers (ensure the view is not obstructed by the wipers). You can use a tape measure to locate the central axis and a spirit level to determine the horizontal line, as shown below:
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=6a8d397257cdeb7eb6f7f0bbbe13f77b)
1.2 Clean the inner surface of the windshield. Remove the protective film from the camera's 3M adhesive and the lens, then mount the camera on the inside of the glass. Ensure the camera is positioned horizontally during installation (a spirit level may be used). After mounting, press firmly for approximately 30 seconds to ensure there are no air bubbles trapped in the 3M adhesive. 1.3 Insert the camera's aviation connector into the video input port (or the video input extension cable port) on the rear panel of the main unit. Typically, this is connected to the CH1 port, though it can be plugged into other ports depending on the specific application scenario; the corresponding channel settings can simply be adjusted later during configuration. Tighten the locking nut to secure the connection.
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=c7ce179252a1428800781d57c2f5d6d3)![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=379be70ad11c58d37caaecc31c5b802d)

###### 2. Enabling Functions
2.1 Open a web browser on your computer, enter the device's local network IP address, input the login password "Adm_123", and click "Login".
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=520b3a9a08ad42bb3275e777ad8d54da)
2.2 Click on the "General Settings" > "AI Settings" menu.
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=048ebdb92a1f469181a74495d3b1a42d)![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=efb0759a081a780d7d85ca0bac87087b)
2.3 In the "AI Settings" menu, enable the ADAS function; connect the ADAS camera to the video input channel on the rear panel of the main unit, then click "Save" to activate the ADAS feature.
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=0281accbf546b9e396a5123e47ab6ea3)

###### 3. Camera Video Configuration
Configure the display for the ADAS camera channel (you may skip this step if the video feed is already visible in the Web ADAS "Vanishing Point" menu).
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=21c0026e623107913c44b2e1d8a2f205)
3.1 Return to the previous level and click "Basic Settings" >>> "Encoding Settings".
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=603aaf46650d3f70b213f1eef6184161)
3.2 Under "Channel Type," select the corresponding resolution for the camera (e.g., "1080P"). This example assumes the ADAS camera is connected to Channel 1 (CH1) of the main unit; confirm and save the settings.![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=fc1938dcc78f73c34623e4b28f334bb2)
Note: The default specification for shipped ADAS cameras is 1080P; please consult your sales representative if changes are required.
3.3 Reboot the device and check if the ADAS channel displays an image.

###### 4. Vanishing Point and Calibration Configuration
4.1 Click the "ADAS Vanishing Point" section in the web menu to open the vanishing point menu. Use the directional keys to move the red crosshair to the horizon line directly in front of the ADAS camera, then click Save to complete the vanishing point calibration.
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=d5dfdcf0986cb26d2e3d536a5488602d)
Note: If the horizontal line of the red crosshair cannot be perfectly aligned with the horizon (the junction of sky and ground) simply by moving it within the menu, use the included L-shaped hex key to loosen the fixing screw on the ADAS camera. Then, gently lift the indicator, slide it to the required scale mark, and retighten the screw. Finally, use the "Up/Down/Left/Right" keys to fine-tune the position so that the red crosshair's horizontal line aligns with the horizon in the distance.
To refresh the ADAS video feed, simply refresh the web interface in your browser.

4.2 Click the "ADAS Calibration" section to open the calibration menu. Enter the measured values for vehicle width, installation height, distance to the left side, distance to the front of the vehicle, and distance to the front wheels, then save the settings. Do not change the default values for lens focal length and sensor size. ![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=43856d61970c783d7804d5f5bfb14e5e)
4.2.1 Vehicle Width:
Use a tape measure to determine the width of the vehicle. This refers to the widest point of the vehicle body, which is typically the distance between the outermost edges of the wheels.
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=9d45461f8f9b83f34b80f8dfbfe6a095)
4.2.2 Installation Height:
Use a tape measure to measure the vertical distance from the ground to the center of the ADAS camera lens.
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=56dcd139d1d62210c65e27d51058ef14)
4.2.3 Distance to Left Side:
Use a tape measure to measure the horizontal distance from the left side of the vehicle to the center of the ADAS camera lens.
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=9ecd1274510dcd279fdfcf57ce6d2ccb)
4.2.4 Distance to Front of Vehicle:
Use a tape measure to measure the distance from the front of the vehicle to the center of the ADAS camera lens. For passenger cars with a protruding front end, this distance must be measured; for vehicles with a flat front end (such as buses or coaches), measurement is not required—simply enter "0" here. 
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=510238c22d763d416714fe0d4687ef83)
4.2.5 Distance to front wheel:
Use a tape measure to measure the distance from the center point of the front wheel to the center of the ADAS camera lens.
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=f654f6daefa1f591b541d4bfe2f88cd5)
If the wheel is located in front of the camera, enter the measured value as a positive number (+).
Example: 580mm![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=b7e5e666ac8421969bc843eb00c29ef7)
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=ec36300b6e93aa5c3b4524210a4abfbd)
If the wheel is located behind the camera, enter the measured value as a negative number (-).
Example: -680mm
After entering the parameters above, click Save.
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=13c68067bc6cfafce6eb27d53bf986c7)

###### 5. Threshold and Sensitivity Adjustment
5.1 In the web menu, navigate to the "ADAS Sensitivity Adjustment" section and enter the speed threshold parameters for HMW (Headway Monitoring Warning), FCW (Forward Collision Warning), LDW (Lane Departure Warning), and PCW (Pedestrian Collision Warning).
Note: An alarm is triggered only when the vehicle speed reaches the configured value for the corresponding alarm type.
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=a9f563a9281afd895fd29d4d23c33e5b)
5.2 Enter the duration threshold values ​​for HMW, PCW, and FCW.
Note: An alarm is triggered when the duration of the corresponding alarm event reaches the configured value; however, for the PCW alarm, the alarm triggers when the duration is *less than* the configured value.
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=63f6696ba061578737ae753c138f1f38)
5.3 Enter the lane departure distance threshold.
Note: This parameter applies to both the left and right lanes. If configured to 0, the alarm triggers when the wheel touches the lane line. If configured to a negative value (e.g., -5), the alarm triggers when the wheel crosses the line by 5 cm. If configured to a positive value (e.g., 5), the alarm triggers when the wheel is 5 cm away from the line. ![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=7ae1504d19af5b6ff6060f60cb72c60e)
5.4 Configure the alarm interval
"ADAS Alarm Interval": For ADAS alarms of the same type (excluding the crosswalk alarm, which is configured separately below), the next alarm will only trigger if the time elapsed since the previous alarm meets or exceeds the configured interval value. Click "Save" after entering the value, then restart the device for the changes to take effect.
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=8121a638bc3370f4ccfd82dbbc1c5b88)

###### 6. Alarm Testing
6.1 Triggering alarms in Test Mode
In the Web menu, navigate to "AI Settings" >>> "Test Mode," then save and restart the device.
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=f11fe252364525badf72fb5f23978538)
6.2 Triggering alarms in Normal Driving Mode: An alarm will trigger when the previously configured thresholds are met, provided the GPS antenna is connected and a GPS fix has been successfully acquired.

6.3 Log in to the V7 client to view alarm information
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=685723b5357825d054a8b9bb4dca02dc)
6.3.1 Real-time preview interface: OSD alarm messages
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=16816bf0ea1d65d4d49d50a8ff26a48c)
6.3.2 Active safety panel: View real-time alarm messages
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=500eb2d3f76ee48f6e95f6894445cdd9)
6.3.3 Active safety menu: View historical alarm messages
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=45c0f4781c31274482347dd756efa077)
